idiom_name: thin DOM listener + pure logic module (Vitest, Testing Library queries)
implementation_notes: The framework-free realization: the event listener reads what it needs from the event target, calls a pure module function and writes the result back, so the DOM part holds no decisions and the module is tested with Vitest without a DOM. What replaces the classic humble class is the module boundary plus the function call; register with addEventListener and remove it again for long-lived elements, and query the remaining shell by role or label rather than by styling selectors.
pitfalls: Handler creep: calculations and conditionals accumulate inside the listener, so the untested part grows with the UI logic; keep the listener to read, call and write.
A module that touches document or window drags the environment back into the logic tests, where a simulated DOM hides the dependency until the code runs in a real browser.
Selectors that encode styling (querySelector('.btn-primary')) pin tests to markup; Testing Library's priority list puts role and label queries first for exactly this reason.

variants.name: React function component + custom hook or reducer
variants.idiom_name: pure function component + custom hook / reducer holding the logic
variants.implementation_notes: The declarative realization: keep components pure - same props, same JSX - and put state and calculations in a custom hook or reducer that tests call directly, following React's rule that side effects belong in event handlers or effects rather than in rendering; the component then only maps state to JSX. Requires React with hooks (16.8+) and rewards the same purity the React strict-mode checks enforce; choose it when the screen is already React, and the DOM-module form otherwise.
pitfalls: Strict Mode intentionally double-invokes component functions in development, so impure render code (writing module state, reading mutable globals) misbehaves exactly where the purity rules were ignored.
Logic left in the component body - derived values computed with side effects, subscriptions - cannot be driven from a test without rendering; move it into the hook or reducer the test calls.
